title: Antler Queen — Yellowjackets
attribution: Costume design: Marie Schley. Photograph: Kailey Schwerman / Paramount+ with SHOWTIME. Production publicity image.
idea: Weathered ivory layers, a loose mesh veil and a compact branching crown.
adapt: Use an oversized ivory knit or thrifted robe as the base. Add a short open-knit veil, a cord belt and soft antlers. Arrange the veil behind or beside your face while dancing. The sculptural outline does most of the work.
rights: Copyrighted film, fashion or photographic reference. Public-domain status and redistribution permission not established.

title: Lottie’s Doomcoming crown — Yellowjackets
attribution: Yellowjackets production still reproduced by Autostraddle. Individual still photographer not identified on the source.
idea: A leaf-and-antler crown over simple clothes, with a trailing lace ribbon.
adapt: Keep your face open: a small crown, muted dress or shirt and trousers, and one ribbon trailing down your back. This is the easiest interpretation of the Yellowjackets reference for a party.
rights: Copyrighted film, fashion or photographic reference. Public-domain status and redistribution permission not established.

title: Dress, Widows of Culloden, autumn/winter 2006–07 — Alexander McQueen
attribution: Alexander McQueen; cream silk tulle and lace with resin antlers. Photograph © Sølve Sundsbø / Art + Commerce, as credited by The Met. Image copy sourced from HuffPost image CDN.
idea: Delicate lace caught on antlers: ghostly, elegant and slightly unsettling.
adapt: An ivory slip, shirt or tunic with a secondhand lace shawl is enough. Use a small antler headband to lift one corner of the fabric. Borrow the contrast of delicate lace and wild branches; the gown and train are optional.
rights: Copyrighted film, fashion or photographic reference. Public-domain status and redistribution permission not established.

title: King Arthur’s halo crown — The Green Knight (2021)
attribution: The Green Knight film still via Natania Barron. Costume design: Malgosia Turzanska; crown development with David Samuel Houghton. Individual still photographer not confirmed.
idea: An aged-gold halo, a dark cloak and a single oversized pendant.
adapt: Cut a small lightweight halo from craft foam, paint it tarnished gold and secure it to a broad headband. A dark shawl with a few metallic fabric patches suggests ceremonial robes. No metal fabrication needed.
rights: Copyrighted film, fashion or photographic reference. Public-domain status and redistribution permission not established.

title: The Green Knight — The Green Knight (2021)
attribution: The Green Knight film still via Natania Barron. Costume design: Malgosia Turzanska; creature prosthetics are a separate effects contribution. Individual still photographer not confirmed.
idea: Bark lines, mossy greens and layered shoulders suggest something ancient.
adapt: Wear brown or charcoal layers with a leaf-covered shoulder or collar. Draw a few branching lines with skin-safe makeup on one cheek. Skip the armor; the texture and asymmetry communicate the creature.
rights: Copyrighted film, fashion or photographic reference. Public-domain status and redistribution permission not established.

title: Faun makeup reference — Pan’s Labyrinth (2006)
attribution: Production makeup photograph reproduced by Monster Legacy. Faun effects: DDT; performer Doug Jones. Individual photographer not identified.
idea: Curved horns, forehead spirals and worn earth tones; strange but beautiful.
adapt: Small curled horns with a brown vest or open shirt and trousers work without a full creature suit. Use forehead spirals or textured cuffs as the extra detail. This photo shows professional makeup: borrow the shapes rather than the whole build.
rights: Copyrighted film, fashion or photographic reference. Public-domain status and redistribution permission not established.

title: Strohmann — Wilder Mann (2010–2011), Charles Fréger
attribution: Photograph © Charles Fréger, Wilder Mann, 2010–2011. Image identified as Strohmann in the photographer’s archive filename.
idea: Pale fringe, a pointed silhouette and one deep-red ribbon.
adapt: Use cream fabric strips as a short shoulder fringe over a simple outfit, then add one oxblood ribbon. Keep the silhouette narrow enough for the apartment. This is a real folk-costume photography reference, not a claim that the pictured tradition is Samhain.
rights: Copyrighted film, fashion or photographic reference. Public-domain status and redistribution permission not established.

title: May Queen floral costume — Midsommar (2019)
attribution: Midsommar production image reproduced by The Independent; individual still photographer not confirmed.
idea: An oversized floral collar translated into rust, wine, cream and dead leaves.
adapt: Our autumn interpretation: cluster a few fabric flowers and leaves on one shoulder or a headband. Repeat the colors in your clothes. The inspiration is floral abundance; you do not need a full flower-covered dress.
rights: Copyrighted film, fashion or photographic reference. Public-domain status and redistribution permission not established.
